catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-riev:
The Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Rievaulx describes the first Cistercian foundation in Yorkshire. Thurston, Archbishop of York, wished for a house of the fervent new order in his diocese, and St. Bernard sent a colony under Abbot William at his invitation.

After some delay Walter Espec became founder and chief benefactor, giving an estate in a wild, lonely valley of the rivulet Rie, ringed by steep hills near Helmsley. The community took possession in 1131, dedicating church and abbey, like all Cistercian houses, to Mary. At first their crude, untilled land left them in want, until Espec's renewed aid and their own incessant labour made it productive.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ernst-von-las: A 1913 entry on Ernst von Lasaulx — the Munich philosopher. Karl Hoeber notes his famous works. The entry preserves his modest fame. His pen served the Catholic schools. A thinker of the nineteenth century. His 1856 works are famed.
